mainQuestion: 按照当前最新的伊朗战争形态，会以哪种形式平息这场战争？
decompositionStrategy: Separate the live conflict into verified facts, escalation drivers, regional impacts, evidence quality, de-escalation conditions, escalation triggers, diplomatic constraints, and disconfirming signals so the final adjudicator can judge the most plausible end-state later.
missingInfo: current date/time for the conflict state
latest reliable sources from official, regional, and independent observers
conflict scope and actors included in the Iran-related war shape

subQuestions.title: Current conflict facts
subQuestions.questionText: What verified events, actors, and military patterns define the current Iran-related conflict shape?
subQuestions.whyItMatters: A final adjudicator cannot judge the likely settlement path without a reliable baseline of what is currently happening.
subQuestions.analysisFocus: Establish the current factual baseline and separate verified conflict facts from stale or propagandistic claims.
subQuestions.scope: Include current observable conflict facts; exclude any final outcome prediction.
subQuestions.expectedAnswerShape: Chronology plus actor and incident table.
subQuestions.omissionRisk: Without this, every later conclusion could rest on an outdated or distorted picture of the conflict.

subQuestions.title: Escalation drivers
subQuestions.questionText: Which incentives and constraints are currently driving escalation or de-escalation among the main actors?
subQuestions.whyItMatters: Settlement forms depend on the incentives pushing actors toward restraint, retaliation, or strategic pause.
subQuestions.analysisFocus: Evaluate military, political, and diplomatic incentives and identify which ones are most likely to move actor behavior.
subQuestions.scope: Include actor incentives and constraints; exclude the final settlement judgment.
subQuestions.omissionRisk: Without this, the final adjudicator may describe possible outcomes without explaining the forces pushing toward them.

subQuestions.title: Regional impact
subQuestions.questionText: Which regional security, economic, and diplomatic impacts could alter the actors' willingness to continue or de-escalate?
subQuestions.whyItMatters: Regional spillovers often create the external pressure that makes a ceasefire, containment, or negotiated pause more or less likely.
subQuestions.analysisFocus: Assess which regional consequences are significant enough to change incentives rather than merely accompany the conflict.
subQuestions.scope: Include regional effects; exclude operational or military recommendations.
subQuestions.expectedAnswerShape: Impact map by actor and channel.
subQuestions.omissionRisk: Without this, the final answer may ignore the costs that can force actors toward restraint or push them toward escalation.

subQuestions.title: Evidence reliability
subQuestions.questionText: Which evidence sources are reliable enough to establish the conflict shape and trend?
subQuestions.whyItMatters: The adjudicator should know which signals deserve confidence and which ones are too weak to drive the final judgment.
subQuestions.analysisFocus: Rank source reliability, corroboration strength, and freshness of evidence across official, regional, and independent reporting.
subQuestions.scope: Include evidence quality and source trustworthiness; exclude the final synthesis itself.
subQuestions.omissionRisk: Without this, weak claims can be overweighted in the final adjudication.

subQuestions.title: De-escalation pathways
subQuestions.questionText: Which variables and conditions would support a ceasefire, negotiated pause, containment, or gradual de-escalation path?
subQuestions.whyItMatters: The final adjudicator must compare concrete path conditions instead of jumping straight to a one-shot final answer.
subQuestions.analysisFocus: Identify the conditions under which each de-escalation path becomes feasible and which path variables matter most.
subQuestions.scope: Include path variables and triggers; exclude any direct probability ranking of the final outcome.
subQuestions.omissionRisk: Without this, the final answer may name a path without the conditions that make it plausible.

subQuestions.title: Escalation triggers
subQuestions.questionText: What risk triggers could invalidate a de-escalation interpretation and shift the conflict toward wider escalation?
subQuestions.whyItMatters: A decision-grade answer needs explicit reversal conditions, not just the current leading interpretation.
subQuestions.analysisFocus: Define the concrete military, diplomatic, or alliance signals that would reverse a de-escalation thesis.
subQuestions.scope: Include escalation triggers and thresholds; exclude military action instructions.
subQuestions.omissionRisk: Without this, the final adjudicator cannot state what evidence would reverse the judgment.

subQuestions.title: Diplomatic constraints
subQuestions.questionText: How do domestic politics, alliances, and back-channel diplomacy constrain each actor's available choices?
subQuestions.whyItMatters: Settlement forms depend not only on battlefield dynamics but also on the political constraints limiting what each actor can accept.
subQuestions.analysisFocus: Assess political and alliance constraints that narrow or widen the plausible settlement set for each actor.
subQuestions.scope: Include political and diplomatic constraints; exclude any final settlement prediction.
subQuestions.omissionRisk: Without this, the final answer may overstate theoretically possible paths that are politically unavailable.

subQuestions.title: Disconfirming evidence
subQuestions.questionText: What evidence would disprove the leading interpretation of the conflict trend and force a reassessment?
subQuestions.whyItMatters: The final adjudicator needs explicit disconfirming signals to keep the eventual judgment falsifiable and honest.
subQuestions.analysisFocus: List the specific contrary signals that would invalidate the current leading interpretation of the conflict trend.
subQuestions.scope: Include reverse conditions and disconfirming evidence; exclude producing the final judgment itself.
subQuestions.omissionRisk: Without this, the final answer may look certain without clearly defining what would prove it wrong.

knownBlindSpots: Real-time battlefield information may still be incomplete.
exhaustivenessCheck.whyNoMoreQuestionsAreNeeded: These eight sub-questions cover the factual baseline, drivers, impacts, evidence quality, path conditions, reversal triggers, political constraints, and disconfirming evidence needed for a later final adjudication.
